answer: Treat every identity as a harbor with a narrow mouth: entry is cheap to request but expensive to clear, because a newcomer must bring a sponsor who stakes real POA on its behavior for a full month. Let trust grow like juniper on stone - slow, rooted, visible - by paying only after several unrelated audits, never on the first answer. Keep the ledger hollow of shortcuts: no bulk join, no delegated proof, no inherited score. A clone ring then faces the same narrow mouth for every copy, and each copy needs a sponsor willing to lose money if it misbehaves.
